candidates.attacker_control: Any attacker-controlled value that a template renders into an <a href="${...}"> (or similar URL attribute) in ContentType.Html mode, e.g. a user-supplied profile/website URL, a return/redirect target, a link provided in user content. The filter is the only URL-scheme defense in the runtime library.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The check is case-insensitive for the literal scheme and tolerates leading whitespace, so 'JavaScript:', ' JAVASCRIPT:' and similar are correctly dropped. Escape.htmlAttribute escapes &, so 'javascript:' style entity obfuscation is neutralized (entities are double-encoded). Quotes are escaped, so attribute break-out is not possible via this path. I checked the documented intent in docs/html-rendering.md (no documented behavior for the javascript: filter, so intent had to be inferred from the check itself and its helper name) and could not confirm whether upstream jte later hardened this helper; there is no runtime execution, no test suite in the snapshot (all tests removed), and no CSP/redirect-policy configuration in the repo that would neutralize the payload.
candidates.impact: Cross-site scripting (script execution in the application's origin) triggered by victim interaction with a link whose href is built from attacker-controlled data; in the common pattern of user-supplied links this becomes stored/reflected XSS. Severity is limited by the need for a user click and by CSP, but the bypass defeats the library's only URL-scheme control.
candidates.prerequisites: Template uses ContentType.Html and places untrusted data in a URL attribute (documented/common usage, e.g. docs/html-rendering.md and docs/index.md show attribute interpolation). The href must be written through the OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput attribute path (single-output smart attribute or an attribute code part), which both map to writeTagAttributeUserContent(). Execution requires a victim click on the poisoned link and no CSP that blocks javascript: navigation. The filter also only covers a/href, so other URL-bearing attributes are unaffected by even the incomplete check.
candidates.root_cause: gg.jte.html.OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.writeTagAttributeUserContent() (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.java:65-75) tries to suppress javascript: URLs, but the underlying check gg.jte.runtime.StringUtils.startsWithIgnoringCaseAndWhitespaces() (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/runtime/StringUtils.java:8-25) only skips whitespace while j == 0, i.e. leading whitespace only; every subsequent character is compared literally. Browsers, when parsing a URL, strip ASCII tab and newline anywhere in the input (and leading C0 control/space characters), so payloads such as "java\tscript:alert(1)", "java\nscript:alert(1)", or "\u0001javascript:alert(1)" are not recognized by the filter. The value then goes through Escape.htmlAttribute (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/escape/Escape.java:25-40), which only escapes ' " & and < — tab/newline/C0 characters are passed through unchanged — so the browser still resolves the attribute to a javascript: URL. The check is additionally narrow: it only applies to tag "a" with attribute "href", leaving other URL sinks (e.g. iframe src, form action, area/link href, object data) with the same class of risk.
candidates.title: javascript: URL filter in OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput is bypassable with embedded tab/newline or leading control characters, allowing XSS via user-controlled href values
candidates.trace: Template link (ContentType.Html) → TemplateParser marks the attribute as a smart attribute / attribute code part (gg/jte/compiler/TemplateParser.java:618-633, 855-918) → JavaCodeGenerator/KotlinCodeGenerator emit jteOutput.setContext("a", "href") + jteOutput.writeUserContent(url) (jte/src/main/java/gg/jte/compiler/java/JavaCodeGenerator.java:316-339) → OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.writeUserContent(String) → writeTagAttributeUserContent(): StringUtils.startsWithIgnoringCaseAndWhitespaces(url, "javascript:") returns false for "java\tscript:..." / "\u0001javascript:..." → Escape.htmlAttribute() escapes only ' " & <, leaving the tab/C0 byte intact → emitted as href="javascript:alert(1)" → browser strips ASCII tab/newline from the URL and navigates/executes the javascript: URL when the link is activated.
candidates.unverified: Browser behavior (stripping of internal ASCII tab/newline and leading C0 controls) was reasoned from the URL/HTML specifications, not executed. Whether upstream jte intends this helper to ignore all whitespace/control characters, and whether a later release hardened it, could not be verified from the snapshot (no git history, no tests). The exact set of URL-bearing attributes an application may use (the check covers only a/href) is application dependent.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS) via incomplete URL scheme validation / sanitizer bypass

coverage_summary: Coverage: all 230 model-visible files were enumerated; I read in full the security-relevant runtime (TemplateEngine, TemplateLoader/RuntimeTemplateLoader/Template, TemplateConfig, CodeResolver, DirectoryCodeResolver/ResourceCodeResolver, TemplateOutput and all output implementations, OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput, Escape, all four HtmlPolicy groups, policies, LocalizationSupport/CssClasses/ForSupport/StringUtils/TemplateUtils/BinaryContent/ClassInfo/Constants/DebugInfo), the compiler/generators (TemplateParser, CodeBuilder, CodeGenerator, ContentProcessor, TemplateCompiler, JavaCodeGenerator, JavaClassCompiler, JavaParamInfo, ClassDefinition/ClassUtils, IoUtils, LineInfo, extension support, MigrateV1To2), the Kotlin module (KotlinCodeGenerator, KotlinClassCompiler, KotlinParamInfo), maven/gradle plugins and tasks, the Spring Boot starter 2/3 autoconfiguration and views, jte-models, jte-native-resources, jte-watcher, jte-extension-api(-mocks), the JSP converter modules (converter classes, Jasper integration JtpParser/JtpConverter, IoUtils), plus build files, docs and GitHub workflows. Escaping behavior in Escape.java and OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput matches the examples/statements in docs/html-rendering.md. Files only skimmed: the duplicate jte-jsp-converter-jakarta module (mirrors the non-jakarta module, spot-checked), some converter helper classes, and repository metadata files.
limitations: The snapshot contains no tests or git history, so upstream intent and any later hardening of the javascript: URL helper could not be verified; the finding rests on source reading plus HTML/URL specification reasoning.

No code was executed, compiled, or fuzzed; the XSS payload behavior (internal tab/newline and leading C0 control stripping by browsers) is reasoned from specification knowledge and is not runtime-confirmed.
Resource/template assets referenced by build files (e.g. jte-models' src/main/jte templates, test/ modules) are absent from the snapshot, so anything they might contribute is uninspected.
Reachability of the candidate depends on application usage (untrusted data in a URL attribute in ContentType.Html mode); no in-repo application code demonstrates that flow end to end.

Other modules (spring starters, plugins, JSP converter) were reviewed for anomalous logic but not exhaustively line-by-line, and dependency versions in poms were not cross-checked against vulnerability databases (no external lookups permitted).

rejected_leads.lead: gg.jte.resolve.DirectoryCodeResolver.resolveRequired()/exists()/getLastModified() (jte/src/main/java/gg/jte/resolve/DirectoryCodeResolver.java:34-59) build the template file path with root.resolve(name) and never canonicalize or verify containment, so a template name containing ../ escapes the template root (arbitrary file read; in OnDemand mode the file content is compiled as Java/Kotlin, which can escalate to code execution if an attacker can also get a crafted file on disk or control file content).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only if an application passes attacker-controlled strings as template names; the CodeResolver contract documents names as template-relative paths ('tag/util/card.jte'), and no in-repo caller (spring starters, maven/gradle plugins) feeds request data into it. Source evidence for an exploitable flow inside this repository is therefore absent, so it is a hardening consideration rather than a demonstrated vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Case-sensitivity mismatch between HTML's case-insensitive attribute names and the runtime check attributeName.startsWith("on") (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.java:70) plus StringUtils.isAllUpperCase() in PreventUppercaseTagsAndAttributes (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/policy/PreventUppercaseTagsAndAttributes.java:13-22): a template using a mixed-case handler name such as OnClick="${x}" passes the default OwaspHtmlPolicy and receives htmlAttribute escaping instead of javaScriptAttribute escaping, so the value is inserted as live JS code in the handler.
rejected_leads.reason: The escaping-mode choice is driven by statically authored template text (attribute name), not by attacker-controlled data, and the mismatch needs an unusual mixed-case handler name in the template. Same weakness exists in PreventInlineEventHandlers (startsWith("on")), which is opt-in. Insufficient evidence of attacker control for a standalone finding.

rejected_leads.lead: OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.writeTagBodyUserContent() (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput.java:57-63) treats only tagName == "script" as a JavaScript context; <style> bodies, and any context where the parser's tag tracking records a non-script tag, fall back to Escape.htmlContent, which does not neutralize CSS metacharacters (CSS injection in style blocks).
rejected_leads.reason: CSS injection in a style block is not script execution, and docs/html-rendering.md lists exactly four escaped contexts (body, attributes, on* attributes, <script> blocks) without naming style, so the observed behavior matches documented intent.

rejected_leads.lead: PreventSingleQuotedAttributes exists (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/policy/PreventSingleQuotedAttributes.java) but is not part of the default OwaspHtmlPolicy (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/html/OwaspHtmlPolicy.java:5-11), and is referenced nowhere else in the snapshot.
rejected_leads.reason: Escape.htmlAttribute escapes both single and double quotes, so single-quoted attributes are not exploitable through the escaping path; the class is plausibly an opt-in policy. No source-backed exploit path.

rejected_leads.lead: HTML context is not propagated across template calls: a @template.foo() call inside an attribute value renders the callee with the same output, and the callee's own setContext("html", null)/setContext(tag, ...) calls can replace the caller's attribute context, so callee output designed for an HTML body could be written unescaped-for-attribute into the caller's attribute (JavaCodeGenerator.onTemplateCall, jte/src/main/java/gg/jte/compiler/java/JavaCodeGenerator.java:424-433).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible design-level context-confusion, but it requires specific cross-template usage patterns (template call inside an attribute) that could not be tied to any attacker-controlled flow with source evidence, and no documentation or test in the snapshot confirms or refutes the behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: ClassInfo/ClassDefinition derive generated class names, package names and file paths from template names (jte-runtime/src/main/java/gg/jte/runtime/ClassInfo.java:11-36, jte/src/main/java/gg/jte/compiler/ClassDefinition.java:63-69), which can produce name collisions or write generated sources at unexpected locations when template names contain dots, dashes or leading dots.
rejected_leads.reason: Names are developer/build-time controlled; '.' is replaced by '/', which blocks ../ traversal in the generated file name. No attacker-controlled path was identified.

summary: Reviewed the jte (Java Template Engine) snapshot (230 model-visible files, version 3.1.16-SNAPSHOT). I traced the HTML output-escaping pipeline end to end: TemplateParser HTML-state tracking (gg/jte/compiler/TemplateParser.java) → Java/Kotlin code generators (setContext emission) → gg.jte.html.OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput dispatch → gg.jte.html.escape.Escape helpers, plus TemplateEngine/TemplateLoader/template-name handling, the maven/gradle plugins, Spring Boot starters, jte-models/native/watcher/extension modules, and the JSP converter. The documented escaping behavior (docs/html-rendering.md) matches the code for HTML bodies, HTML attributes and on* attributes. The strongest source-supported issue is the URL-scheme (javascript:) control in OwaspHtmlTemplateOutput: its helper only skips whitespace at index 0 and does not treat ASCII tab/newline (or leading C0 controls) as ignorable, while browsers strip those characters when parsing URLs — so a value like "java\tscript:alert(1)" or "\u0001javascript:..." passes the check and is emitted (htmlAttribute only neutralizes quotes/&/<), yielding a click-triggered XSS in `<a href="${userValue}">`. That is one candidate; other plausible-but-weaker leads are listed as rejected.
